title: Titanium Bleed Air Duct

alloyReason: Grade 9 Ti-3Al-2.5V (UNS R56320) is specified for Titanium Bleed Air Duct where intermediate strength between CP titanium and Ti-6Al-4V is needed with superior cold formability. Its 620 MPa tensile strength with 20% elongation enables 30% weight reduction versus steel while allowing tube bending and flaring without intermediate annealing — critical for Engine bleed air duct (Grade 9 Ti tube) requiring complex-formed geometries. This rationale is driven by engine bleed air duct (grade 9 ti tube) and fat life requirements.

Wire EDM contour profiling with Class 6g gauge
CMM per AS9102 with Class 6g gauge
surfaceTreatment: Shot peening Almen 0.008-0.012A inducing compressive residual stress for extended HCF life in aerospace service — tailored for engine bleed air application
commonFailures: Fretting fatigue at dovetail interface - mitigated by shot peen Almen 0.008A + dry-film lubricant coating — critical for engine bleed air performance

faq.q: What corrosion protection is needed for Titanium Bleed Air Duct in aerospace environments?
faq.a: Grade 9 Ti-3Al-2.5V naturally forms a protective TiO₂ passive layer that requires no additional coating for corrosion resistance in standard aerospace environments. For engine bleed air exposed to hydraulic fluids (Skydrol), de-icing fluids, or marine atmosphere, the passive layer is sufficient. However, galvanic isolation from carbon fiber composites (via fiberglass ply or PTFE sleeve) is required to prevent hydrogen embrittlement.

faq.q: What material certifications are provided with Titanium Bleed Air Duct?
faq.a: Each Titanium Bleed Air Duct shipment includes EN 10204 Type 3.1 mill test certificate with chemical analysis, mechanical properties, and heat identification. Dimensional inspection reports and Certificate of Conformance (CoC) are standard. First Article Inspection Reports (FAIR) per AS9102 are available on request for engine bleed air.
